title: Range Sum Queries
statement:
You are given an array `a` of `n` integers and `q` queries. Each query gives two indices `s` and `e` (0-indexed, both inclusive, `s ≤ e`) and asks for the sum `a[s] + a[s + 1] + ... + a[e]`.

The array never changes between queries, so all `q` queries refer to the same array. Answer every query, in the order given.
inputFormat:
The first line contains `n` and `q`.
The second line contains the `n` integers of the array.
Each of the next `q` lines contains two integers `s` and `e`.
outputFormat: Print `q` lines; line `i` holds the answer to the `i`-th query.

examples.explanation: Query (2, 3) sums 3 + 6 = 9. Query (0, 4) sums 1 + 2 + 3 + 6 + 3 = 15. Query (1, 2) sums 2 + 3 = 5.
The whole array sums to -5 + 4 - 1 = -2. A query with s = e is just that single element, 4.

hints: Summing the range from scratch for each query costs O(n) per query, which is too slow when both n and q are large.
Since the array never changes, you can do the heavy work once, before reading any query.
Store prefix sums, where `pre[i]` is the sum of the first `i` elements. A range sum is then a difference of two prefix values.
